correctness.rationale: For every N>=5 and every k=1..4, the proof reduces the retained operator to 2I-UU*, diagonalizes the two-basis erased Gram block, handles every r+s=k split, explicitly optimizes the 2-by-2 phase t=(a-b)(c-d), proves the unique prime/composite equality conditions, and counts masks with an exact ordered-pair argument. The N=4 failure boundary is verified. Direct numerical replay enumerated 55365 masks and 18336 full spectra at N=5..13, but the infinite claim relies on the algebraic proof.

originality.rationale: Targeted semantic published-finding corpus queries, the accessible own ledger claims, three primary arXiv papers and three full published-result manuscripts were compared by objects, hypotheses, implication and equality patterns. No inspected source covers the precise sharp all-N first prime/composite four-deletion stability theorem or its complete mask counts. The 2-by-2 Fourier and principal-angle reductions are standard, not claimed as new; residual bibliographic risk is explicitly retained.
residual_risks: A general theorem on 2-by-2 Fourier-minor singular values or pairs of orthonormal bases could imply some or all of the result under a different terminology; no exhaustive worldwide literature guarantee.
The standard two-projection spectral reduction is textbook background; originality is assessed only for the exact prime/composite erasure optimization, incidence and first-threshold classification.

The 2015 Larson–Scholze chapter on bridging erasures in unions of two bases was available only as an abstract; a theorem hidden in its full text might be relevant, though no decisive equivalent claim is apparent from accessible material.

value.rationale: The union of the coordinate and Fourier bases is the canonical twice-redundant MUB frame. The theorem establishes, for infinitely many dimensions, the first erasure cardinality at which factorization of N changes the worst recovery stability, determines the sharp singular-value loss and all equality masks, and gives exact arithmetic incidence counts. It is a natural complete reconstruction-stability invariant, not an arbitrary slice or a minor numerical improvement; it does not claim optimality among all frames.
